smell: SetupKubeconfig performs filesystem I/O (FileExists, env mutation) but omits context.Context, while every other exported method on *Phase (Execute, DeployInfrastructure, WaitForBootstrap, MonitorInstallation, SetupClusterAccess, StartWorkerVMs, ValidateClusterAccess) takes ctx first. The asymmetry blocks callers from cancelling the sequence uniformly and breaks the ctx-first discipline on the exported Phase surface.
severity_reason: Minimal current-harm (filesystem op is fast) but the signature is out of family with sibling Phase methods and blocks future I/O (e.g., writing a sentinel) from honoring cancellation.
fix_summary: Change signature to `func (p *Phase) SetupKubeconfig(ctx context.Context, clusterDir string) error`. Update the single call site in internal/distribution/okd/install/steps.go to pass ctx. Matches SetupClusterAccess in the same phase (which takes ctx even though it currently ignores it).
rule_source: Google Go Style Guide §Contexts ('context.Context should be the first argument of exported functions that do I/O or may block')
must_preserve: Canonical call site at install/steps.go StepSetupKubeconfig; must still mutate p.Exec.Env so downstream subprocesses inherit KUBECONFIG.

smell: Minimum control-plane resource constants live in two packages with the same values but diverging disk-size number. okd.MinControlPlaneDiskGB=50 matches config.MinDiskGBControlPlaneOKD=50 so the okd constants exist only so Validate can produce a different error message — config already validates resources during load. Two sources of truth for the same limit.
severity_reason: Both sets currently agree; but a future OKD-version bump will almost certainly update one and drift. config package is the canonical location (it already runs the validator during loader.LoadFile).
fix_summary: Delete okd.MinControlPlane* constants and Provisioner.Validate's resource-min checks; rely on config.ValidateOKDConfig which is already invoked via cfg.Validate() during setup. Alternatively import config.MinCPUControlPlaneOKD / MinMemoryMBControlPlaneOKD / MinDiskGBControlPlaneOKD in okd.Validate. Net: one constant set.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'a little copying is better than a little dependency' — but only when copies don't drift; here they will
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (BasePhase/config as single sources of truth)
must_preserve: All three numeric values (8192, 4, 50) must remain the enforced minimum — just declared once.

smell: firewall.Configure and firewall.RemoveRules are exported but every in-tree caller uses the okd-specific wrappers ConfigureOKD / RemoveOKDRules. RemoveRules(HAProxyFrontendPorts(), ...) is the one exception — a single call in postinstall/haproxy.go. Configure has no direct caller. The pair is shaped like a 'future distro swap' API; flag as scaffolding but note Configure is unreferenced.
severity_reason: Scaffolding-shaped: if Configure exists, RemoveRules stays; they map to a future 'configure arbitrary port set' CLI path (symmetric API).
fix_summary: Verify intent — are Configure/RemoveRules expected entry points for a future non-OKD distro? If yes, keep and document the layering. If no, inline Configure into ConfigureOKD and keep RemoveRules (still has one external caller).
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API: Configure exists, RemoveRules stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (package-level helpers live in producer pkg)
must_preserve: validatePort allowlist; both wrappers' current behavior.

smell: cleanup.GenerateSummary and cleanup.Summary struct are exported but the only caller is the package-private printSummary(). No external caller. The function is shaped like a public status-query but without a symmetric sibling (no cleanup.Verify or similar), so it does not cleanly fit scaffolding.
severity_reason: Possibly shaped for a future `okdctl cleanup status` CLI verb; defer to owner rather than deleting. No correctness impact.
fix_summary: Either unexport (GenerateSummary -> generateSummary, Summary -> summary) if no CLI surface planned, or keep both exported and add a one-line doc-comment pointing to the intended caller (e.g. 'used by okdctl cleanup status; see roadmap.md').
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')
MEMORY.md §scaffolding (not symmetric — no matching verb in cleanup/)
must_preserve: The current behavior when printSummary runs at the end of Execute.

smell: OKDVersionFetcher.GetLatestForMinor is exported with no caller. GetLatestStable (paired sibling) has none either — only FetchVersions is called. Both are shaped like a symmetric-API trio (FetchVersions / GetLatestStable / GetLatestForMinor) for a future `okdctl releases list --minor 4.18` verb.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: symmetric API with a single consumed member (FetchVersions). Future CLI verb 'releases latest' is a plausible caller.
fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md — if a `okdctl releases latest [--minor N.M]` command is planned, keep both. Otherwise demote to private helpers. Do not delete without checking with owner.
must_preserve: FetchVersions (has a caller) and the disk cache behavior.

smell: OKDVersion.ShortVersion is exported with no caller in the repo. DisplayName and Major/Minor are used by wizard/steps and cli/releases; ShortVersion is not. Shaped like a symmetric 'version formatting' trio but currently standalone.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: symmetric with DisplayName/Major/Minor (all are view helpers on OKDVersion).
fix_summary: Verify — if docs/releases plan a short-form version display, keep. If not, delete. No API impact either way because ShortVersion has zero external references.

smell: Phase.ValidateClusterAccess, Phase.SetupClusterAccess, Phase.SetupKubeconfig are exported on *Phase in the install package. The only callers are the same package's steps.go. Since Phase is itself exported and these are phase-public methods called by a user-facing `okd.Provisioner`, they fit a future-CLI-verb shape ('okdctl cluster access', 'okdctl kubeconfig-setup'). Flagged as scaffolding.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: shaped like future-CLI-verb (e.g. `okdctl cluster access verify`). Keeping per MEMORY.md §scaffolding.
fix_summary: Verify intent — do any planned subcommands call these? If yes, keep exported and document. If no, unexport (validateClusterAccess) to reduce package surface.
must_preserve: The step.go callers' behavior; the deploy-time chown semantics in SetupClusterAccess.

smell: setup.DefaultOptions has the Default* naming pattern common for 'zero-arg constructor of a defaulted options struct'. Other phase packages use NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot). The same repo mixes: postinstall.DefaultTimeout (constant, fine), install.DefaultBootstrapTimeout (constant), but setup.DefaultOptions (function). A reader can't tell whether Default* prefixed symbols are values or functions at a glance.
severity_reason: Naming consistency. Rename to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and the three *Options factories all share the same name.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions -> setup.NewOptions; accept (cfg, projectRoot) and fold ResolveReleaseBaseURL call inside. Single call site in okd.go updates. Aligns with opt-inconsistent-cfg-opts finding.
rule_source: Go naming convention: `New*` for constructors; `Default*` for values

smell: Three call sites hardcode the family strings "rhel" / "debian" despite the platform package defining familyRHEL and familyDebian constants for exactly this purpose. The constants are unexported, so leaking string literals here also hints at a package-boundary issue.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: consistency/typo-risk rather than active bug; relates to CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes on canonical helpers
fix_summary: Export FamilyRHEL and FamilyDebian from internal/platform and use the constants at the three sites. Also expose a DefaultOS() helper so the fallback is not assembled inline (the "rhel default" assumption appears twice).

smell: Two functions build a display status string via the same switch on (Skipped/Success/default) producing the literal values "skip"/"ok"/"fail". The value set is a three-state enum spelled inline in two places; adding a fourth state (e.g. "partial") would require editing both.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: duplicated 3-way switch producing stringly-typed output across two functions within the same file
fix_summary: Introduce a StepResult.DisplayStatus() method returning a typed StatusLabel (or even a plain stepStatus enum with a String() method) so callers write `sb.kv(string(s.StepID), fmt.Sprintf("%-4s  %s", s.DisplayStatus(), d))` once. Or hoist the switch into a local helper in summary.go.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §code-comments (rubric favoring extraction when switch repeats)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: CSR.Pending is a boolean field that is unconditionally set to `true` by its only constructor (cluster.PendingCSRs) and never read anywhere. It is named to suggest tri-state (Pending/Approved/Denied) but the producer only emits Pending rows. Either the field is dead, or the CSR type should grow to carry the full conditions slice.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: field has no downstream reader and conveys no information — removing it is a one-line drop but the type is exported, so a consumer edit may be required
fix_summary: Delete the `Pending bool` field and the `Pending: true` assignment. The type name and constructor already convey that every returned CSR is pending. If a future consumer needs to distinguish states, introduce a CSRState enum (Pending/Approved/Denied) rather than a bool.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: AddonInfo.Category is populated by the two catalog addons ("gitops", "secrets") but is not read anywhere in the codebase. It is a stringly-typed metadata field reserved for a future grouping UI. If that UI is on the roadmap, keep it as scaffolding; if not, it is dead weight encouraging ad-hoc values.
fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md. If a category-grouped wizard/list is planned, keep the field and add a typed AddonCategory enum (gitops/secrets/storage/…) so callers can't typo "gitops " or "git-ops". If not, drop the field.

smell: LogLevel is a custom enum (Debug/Info/Warn/Error) that is not referenced anywhere — the package exposes Debug()/Info()/Warn()/Error() functions directly and uses charmlog.Level for level parsing. The enum is a premature abstraction that shadows log/slog's own leveling.
evidence:
type LogLevel int

const (
    LogLevelDebug LogLevel = iota
    LogLevelInfo
    LogLevelWarn
    LogLevelError
)
fix_summary: Delete the LogLevel type and its four constants. Callers wanting a typed level should import log/slog.Level directly (LevelDebug/LevelInfo/LevelWarn/LevelError) — that's also the seam audit-modernization will push toward.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: retrieveProvisionResult hardcodes the VM name literals "bootstrap", and uses Sprintf patterns `"master%d"` / `"worker%d"` for the other roles. The role *values* ARE typed (RoleBootstrap/RoleMaster/RoleWorker), but the *names* duplicate the string — so `Name: "bootstrap"` and `Role: RoleBootstrap` sit side by side and can drift. setup/nodes.go repeats the pattern.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: Name and Role are parallel stringly-typed channels; rename one and they diverge silently
fix_summary: Use the role constant as the name prefix: `Name: fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", RoleMaster, i)` and `Name: string(RoleBootstrap)`. Or add a VMRole.NodeName(index int) helper so the single-source-of-truth is the VMRole type.

smell: Default CPU type is the bare literal "host" with no named constant. The surrounding file has 50-default-gb and "virtio" literals as well (lines 33, 121); together they form a small cluster of config-shaped defaults that belong in a `defaults` block alongside Topology/Networking.
fix_summary: Define `const DefaultProxmoxCPUType = "host"` (and similarly DefaultNetworkModel = "virtio", DefaultOSDiskGB = 50) either in terraform.go or in an internal/config/defaults.go extension, and reference the constant. Matches the existing constant block at internal/config/constants.go.

smell: The if/else-if/else ladder around token assembly has an `else if px.TokenID != ""` branch whose `if` branch explicitly does nothing (`_ = px.TokenID`). The comment explains the semantic (avoid "tokenid=tokenid=secret" double-prefix), but the empty-but-for-a-side-channel branch is an anti-pattern — invert the condition and return early, or drop the branch if the semantic is already covered by the else-if.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: semantic is correct but the shape (empty-then-else) is the kind of thing linters flag when they pick up the idiom
fix_summary: Collapse to: `if px.TokenID != "" && !strings.Contains(px.APIToken, "=") { token = px.TokenID + "=" + px.APIToken }`. Same behavior, no empty branch, no `_ = px.TokenID` dummy to confuse future readers.

smell: Package cli has two separate '// Package cli ...' doc blocks (root.go:1-4 and confirm.go:1-3) with overlapping but non-identical summaries. Go concatenates both into godoc, producing two paragraphs that re-introduce the package twice. CLAUDE.md §code-comments item 1 calls for one block of 1-3 sentences; splitting it across files violates that shape.
fix_summary: Keep the root.go block (it carries the exit-code contract callers care about); demote confirm.go's leading comment to a regular non-package doc comment that describes promptForConfirmation, not the package. Alternative: merge both summaries into root.go and strip confirm.go's // Package cli header.
must_preserve: The exit-code contract (codes 2/3/4/5/1/130/0) in root.go must survive in whichever block is kept.

smell: Package platform has two '// Package platform ...' doc blocks (platform.go:1-5 and packages.go:1-7). godoc shows both — the first block explicitly says 'see platform.go for the package summary' which is a godoc anti-pattern (the reader is already reading godoc, not the source). Package doc should live in one file.
evidence: // Package platform — see platform.go for the package summary. This file\n// implements the OS-agnostic PackageManager abstraction, with a single\n// Manager type driven by per-family binary names (dnf/apt-get, rpm/dpkg)
fix_summary: Strip the '// Package platform' prefix from packages.go and leave the existing file-scoped commentary as a plain block comment (or delete it — the body is self-explanatory). platform.go keeps the sole package-level block.
rule_source: Effective Go §Commentary — package comment 'appears in the first file of the package that has a comment'
must_preserve: The factual content about Manager's stderr-capture design — move it to a comment on the Manager type itself if it needs a home.

smell: Executor only sets cmd.Env when len(e.Env) > 0, otherwise the subprocess inherits the parent's full environment — including PROXMOX_PASSWORD, PULL_SECRET, PROXMOX_API_TOKEN, and any other credentials the operator exported. A bug or malicious wrapper in terraform / openshift-install / oc plugins could leak these into argv-visible children (e.g. via /proc/self/environ readable by same-uid processes).
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — every exec.Command call that doesn't explicitly configure env inherits credentials; the canonical wrapper is the place to fix this once.
fix_summary: Always set cmd.Env explicitly. Build a minimal base (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, KUBECONFIG, PROXMOX_*, TF_* allowlist) via an env-allowlist applied by default. Extend WithEnv to be additive on top of the allowlist rather than optional. Document the escape hatch WithInheritedEnv for the one or two callers (doctor, install monitor) that legitimately need full inheritance.
must_preserve: KUBECONFIG propagation used by install.SetupKubeconfig; TerraformEnv plumbing via WithEnv; password-scrubbing invariants in internal/credentials.

smell: configureSELinuxForApache discards both the result and error of two semanage port invocations via '_, _ = p.Exec.Run(...)'. The comment 'Try -a first; if port already exists, -m modifies' covers the expected case, but any other semanage failure (policy not loaded, selinux in disabled state, perms) is invisible — apache then silently binds 8080 with no SELinux label and may later refuse connections.
fix_summary: Capture result of the -m call and log result.Stderr at warn level if exit != 0. The -a fallback-to-error pattern is fine, but the final state should be checked; a single 'semanage port -l | grep 8080' probe would confirm the policy was applied and surface any real failure.
rule_source: Go proverb: errors are values — handle them
repo counter-example: p.Log.Warn on apache.configureApachePort failures
must_preserve: the -a then -m ordering (first-add-then-modify) must stay to handle both fresh and pre-labeled hosts.

smell: NewInsecure returns an HTTP client with InsecureSkipVerify=true, narrowly scoped to bootstrap-phase probes per the doc comment. No test locks that New() does NOT return an insecure client (i.e. the TLS config is nil or has InsecureSkipVerify=false). A refactor that factories out a shared transport could silently flip the invariant.
severity_reason: The invariant "New() is secure" is intuitive but worth locking. A regression would defeat TLS verification on every HTTP call the repo makes — but the caller landscape is small and the gosec suppression is present, so the blast radius is bounded.
fix_summary: TestNewVsNewInsecure: c := New(1*time.Second); assert c.Transport is nil (Go uses DefaultTransport which validates); d := NewInsecure(1*time.Second); assert d.Transport.(*http.Transport).TLSClientConfig.InsecureSkipVerify is true. Three assertions, no live network.
must_preserve: New() has no custom Transport; NewInsecure() HAS InsecureSkipVerify=true.
